paragraphs.text: Beeble is a creature type describing a magical construct similar to a Homunculus , which is used by the researchers of the Tolarian Academy as a convenient, easily summoned demonstration subject.

Beebles are small, slightly larger than a fist, have bare, rounded bodies ranging in color from pink to grey-blue, and a set of feathered wings. They are permanently cheerful, even infuriatingly so, mischievous but not maliciously so, and seemingly indestructible (though they can be unsummoned). Because of their irritating and bewildering nature, students loved to use Beebles in practical jokes, and Teferi once tied a pair to his feet to bounce tremendous distances.
Currently, all printed beebles are mono- blue

Beebles are based on artist Jeff Miracola 's cover for The Duelist #22, where Squee was harassed by small, round pink creatures. Miracola reused them as depiction of souls on the card Equilibrium ( Exodus ). Miracola's creature design inspired Mark Rosewater to concept a card for Urza's Legacy featuring them that would see print as Bouncing Beebles . For Urza's Destiny , Mark designed a second card himself, Bubbling Beebles . Beebles are depicted on a small number of other cards, including Donate ( Urza's Destiny ), Wizard Mentor ( Urza's Saga ), and the Exodus version of Nausea .

After Urza's Destiny was released, Wizards of the Coast decided that Beebles were a bit sillier in tone than the general tone they wanted to express in Magic: The Gathering . Beebles subsequently ceased being included on black bordered cards. It is unclear exactly when this change in stance occurred, but the flavor text of Bursting Beebles ( Unhinged ) claims that "... the beebles quit Magic for several years following the release of the Mercadian Masques set. "

Mark, remaining a fan of the Beeble, used his position as lead designer of Un-sets to keep the creature type around. Across the Un-sets, Beebles have returned on Bursting Beebles ( Unhinged ), Blurry Beeble ( Unstable ), and Bamboozling Beeble ( Unfinity ). In Unhinged they were also used in the art of Topsy Turvy and Sauté , and in the flavor text of Fraction Jackson . Unsanctioned promoted Beebles to the status of planeswalker with B.O.B. (Bevy of Beebles) and included a Beeble token , while Unfinity featured Pick-a-Beeble .

Rosewater has continued to reiterate that Beebles fall outside the tone of Magic since the original decision, even naming the Rosewater Scale for creature types the " Beeble Scale " as the likelihood of the type returning on a Standard -legal card is a 10 out of 10 ("I never say never, but this would require a major miracle"). While unlikely to return as part of regular Magic , Mark has stated that Beebles were are a usable option for supplemental products, though none aside from Un-sets have used them.
